page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 28 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It is configured with 224 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. The instance supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic and vector instructions, but lacks AVX-512 extensions.

The instance delivers strong compute performance across multi-threaded operations. In benchmark testing, the c2d-standard-56 achieves an upper-quartile stress-ng multi-core score of 82,121.09 and a PassMark CPU score of 63,148.67. High-concurrency operations show solid throughput, with Clang software compilation reaching 42,226.0 and ray tracing scoring 62,635.0 in Geekbench suites. Memory subsystem benchmarks reveal 3,877.36 GB/sec cached small-block read bandwidth and a PassMark memory score of 3,124.78, ranking within the top tier. However, uncached sustained memory access settles into median tiers, logging 137.27 GB/sec for large-block reads and 68.92 GB/sec for writes.

Hardware tradeoffs are centered on storage and acceleration options. The instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external network block storage volumes for persistent data. Furthermore, complementary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned by default.

Given its high core count, reliable multithreading scalability, and balanced memory allocation, the c2d-standard-56 is well suited for CPU-bound enterprise workloads. Recommended applications include large-scale CI/CD software build pipelines, distributed database operations, batch image and video processing, and CPU-based lightweight language model inferencing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized instance provisioned with 56 dedicated vCPUs and 224 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 28 physical cores and 2 threads per core, the configuration offers a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top quartile for multi-core compute capability, achieving a stress-ng score of 82,121.09, alongside top-tier cached memory throughput. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, utilizing network-attached persistent disks for all non-volatile storage. With cryptographic instruction support and strong throughput in compilation and database tasks, c2d-standard-56 is targeted at compute-heavy batch workloads, automated build and compilation farms, and multi-threaded enterprise application hosting.
